features/calendar.manual: Calendar and activity drafts, recurrence and page design use explicit grants and current versions. Publishing requires calendar:publish and an explicit request. Archive/restore of published items, subscription and delivery settings, and external feeds require the calendar workspace; native publication can trigger subscriber updates.

features/cms.manual: Page copies, languages, revision restoration and draft menus/appearance require explicit management/settings grants. Publishing exact saved content or settings needs website:publish and an explicit request. Menu-only publication preserves published appearance; dependencies and images never publish automatically. The cookie-only website review coordinates existing services atomically with per-item form/file consent; delegated REST/MCP publication retains separate exact-target operations and scopes. Archiving one ordinary single-language club page requires website:manage plus website:publish, explicit removal intent, a current revision and no draft/published homepage/menu/Events references; history is retained, with no direct unarchive. Multilingual/shared/event archival, hard deletion, timed publication, template installation and executable code require staff workflows. New website:organize plus website:write permit draft hierarchy, independent slugs and reusable sections. Combined visual preview checks exact saved page, settings and shared draft revisions.

features/events.manual: New explicit operational, registration, guest and access grants support requested version-checked actions directly through existing services. Existing events:prepare grants stay draft-only. Provider setup, checkout activation, payments, entries and draws remain outside automation. V1 review proposals are retired in v2.

features/forms.manual: Form definitions retain separate grants from private responses, status updates, exports, deletion, recipients and retention. Direct requests require current form/event authority and exact versions or selection fingerprints. Registration history cannot be deleted. Webhooks remain administration-only.

features/projects.manual: Project stories use separate read/write/publication grants and current versions. Requested archive, restore and unpublication require the new projects:manage opt-in and commit receipts atomically. Cover media must already be public; dependencies never publish automatically. Feature availability remains a staff workflow. Projects do not manage volunteer identities, attendance or registration.

features/guests.manual: Private guest reads and exact-source access grants/revocations need separate opt-in scopes, event authority and recent identity for access changes. Claiming guest access and sending invitations remain native authenticated workflows; no login bypass.

features/media.manual: REST/MCP uploads, source imports and edited copies stay private; administration uploads default public with an explicit private option. Separate media:manage and files:manage opt-ins permit requested metadata editing, atomic organization/hiding/deletion and image copies, with current fingerprints and protected retained references. Existing image grants do not widen. Publication remains separately granted and never publishes dependencies. Files and albums have independent grants; image permissions never imply private document/audio/video access. Mutations use atomic receipts; upload chunks/finalization/cancellation reuse durable actor-bound sessions.

features/members.manual: Separate opt-in grants cover private member metadata, membership decisions, staff roles and owner access. Current authority, exact membership version and recent identity are required for changes; no self-escalation or last-owner removal. Authentication policy and credentials remain administration-only.

features/partners.manual: Publishing saved profiles needs directory:publish and an explicit request; images must already be public. directory:manage separately permits requested draft restoration and reference-protected unpublication. Receipt payloads exclude event placement names whose access may later change. Contacting partners remains outside automation.

integrations/automation.manual: REST and MCP have separate transport switches and credentials. Existing grants never widen. New private-data and operational grants require opt-in and fresh consent. Requested actions execute directly; receipts share domain transactions and recheck authority on replay. Task labels group completed operations, not background jobs. Resets invalidate generations and clear private receipt/export payloads. Connection management, provider setup and resets remain administration/maintenance-only.

integrations/email.manual: Explicit grants permit shared template draft/publication and retrying failed native form alerts to configured recipients. Queued is not delivered. Provider credentials, sender setup, arbitrary mail and campaigns remain outside automation.

integrations/google.manual: Provider credentials, domain policy and Google session verification require staff configuration. Platform-wide login policy and appearance are human-managed Settings; REST and MCP never change authentication policy.

integrations/luma.manual: Provider credentials, synchronization, participant data and purchases require approved provider workflows.

integrations/ui.manual: Presentation of integration settings; has no separate automation action.

core.manual: Identity is readable through website_context. Installation, domains, authentication policy and feature switches remain manual. Explicit ownership scope can authorize requested membership owner changes through current native authority; it never permits self-escalation.

infrastructure.manual: Storage, databases, encryption and delivery adapters have no direct automation interface.

composition.manual: Composition wires shared services into REST and MCP; it must not bypass service authorization.

app/api.manual: Legacy cookie APIs remain staff workflows. Only explicitly registered v1 operations are callable through automation.

../db/schema.manual: Schema changes require review of DTOs, migrations, scopes and both automation interfaces.

app/automation-preview.manual: One-use internal rendering only. Scripts and external requests are blocked; saved private media requires explicit inspection authority.
